title: The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms
abstract: Proves the finite-dimensional Hanson-Wright concentration inequality for quadratic forms of independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian real random variables whose maximum least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scale is positive, for matrices with positive Frobenius and operator norms. The bound uses the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2). This is the MGF normalization of the usual result; no formal identification with an Orlicz psi-2 norm is claimed. The development derives the required moment-generating-function certificate instead of assuming it, and contributes reusable scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum infrastructure.

informal.LeanPool.HansonWright.hanson_wright_ineq: For independent mean-zero real random variables with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales and positive maximum coordinate MGF scale, and a matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, the centered quadratic form satisfies the Hanson-Wright two-regime exponential tail bound with the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2).
informal.LeanPool.HansonWright.hasHansonWrightMGF: Given positive K and operator norm and C at least 64 * exp(1)^2, independent coordinates with global-MGF sub-Gaussian parameter K^2 satisfy the local quadratic cumulant-generating-function estimate needed for Hanson-Wright.
informal.LeanPool.bernstein_inequality: A finite family of independent, centered, uniformly bounded real random variables satisfies the classical scalar Bernstein tail inequality.
